title: About 85% of three-color totalistic cellular automata behave regularly

fields.label: Label
fields.value: About 85% of three-color totalistic cellular automata behave regularly

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: About 85% of the 2187 three-color nearest-neighbor totalistic cellular automata produce behavior that is ultimately quite regular, while the remainder include rules with seemingly random behavior and rules with interacting localized structures like rule 110.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 3: The World of Simple Programs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: About 85% of all three-color totalistic cellular automata produce behavior that is ultimately quite regular.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 3, “The World of Simple Programs”; section “More Cellular Automata” (from p. 53), p. 65. Scope: three-color nearest-neighbor totalistic cellular automata from a single gray cell

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch03-05: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.93

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The complete rule space is small enough for exhaustive modern computation. Qualitative edge cases require classification choices, but the numerical prevalence and cited behavior types are directly checkable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate all 2187 three-color nearest-neighbor totalistic rules from one gray cell and classify trajectories using stated periodicity, randomness, and localized-structure criteria. The exact regular fraction can then be compared with 85 percent and exceptional classes inspected.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ultimately regular may require long transients or proofs.

Random-looking and rule-110-like need operational thresholds.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The population size, 2187, is small, and each evolution is a nearest-neighbor totalistic rule that standard software already runs. The 85 percent figure is approximate and can be reproduced or missed by a uniform classifier. A few rules in the source itself resolve only after thousands of steps, which is still inside a weeks-scale rerun.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Simulate all 2187 three-color nearest-neighbor totalistic rules from a single gray cell for a horizon of many thousands of steps, and label each as ultimately periodic or nested, apparently random, or structure-forming. The claim is confirmed if about 85 percent fall in the regular class, and refuted if the regular share is far from 85 percent once long transients are included.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ultimately regular can be hidden by transients of thousands of steps, so the horizon has to be long and the holdouts inspected.

A minority of rules may still be ambiguous at any practical cutoff.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.85
data adequacy: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.8

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: When all 2187 three-colour nearest-neighbour totalistic cellular automata are run from a single gray cell for a few thousand steps, about 85 % produce patterns whose late-time central region is time-periodic or compresses like classical nested patterns, and the remaining 15 % or so compress like random or class-4 (localised-structure) patterns.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py ran all 2187 three-colour totalistic codes from a single gray cell for T = 3000 steps on an array of width 2*(T+128)+1 (boundaries cannot reach the centre), then classified the central 128-column strip: time-periodic with p <= 256 over rows 2250..2999, or lzma compressibility rho over rows 1500..2999 below tau. Calibration before the census: nested references rho = 0.017..0.037 (Pascal mod 2 / mod 3, Thue-Morse and period-doubling outer products), irregular references rho = 0.099..0.136 (elementary rules 110, 124, 137, 193) and 1.11..1.12 (rules 30, 45); classes separated, tau = sqrt(0.0367 * 0.0985) = 0.0601. Result: 1706 codes periodic, 145 non-periodic but nested-compressible (rho <= 0.042), 336 irregular (rho 0.12..1.11, median 0.90; 169 with rho >= 0.9); regular fraction 1851/2187 = 0.8464, inside the pre-registered [0.80, 0.90] band.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Each code c in 0..2186 (Wolfram's convention: base-3 digit k of c is the new colour for neighbourhood sum k in 0..6; colours 0 = white, 1 = gray, 2 = black) is run for T = 3000 steps from a single gray cell on a white background with an array wide enough that boundary effects cannot reach the central 128 columns. Statistics on the central strip (columns -64..63): (i) periodic: rows 2250..2999 are time-periodic with some period p <= 256; (ii) rho = 8 * lzma_bytes / (cells * log2(3)) over rows 1500..2999. Calibration (performed before the codes are run): nested references are the same-size strips of Pascal's triangle mod 3 (3 symbols), Pascal's triangle mod 2, and the Thue-Morse and period-doubling outer-product patterns (normalised by log2 of their own alphabet size); irregular references are the strips of elementary rules 110, 124, 137, 193 (localised structures) and 30, 45 (random) run from a single black cell with the same geometry. tau = geometric mean of the largest nested-reference rho and the smallest irregular-reference rho. A code is 'regular' iff it is periodic or rho < tau. 'supports' if the regular fraction lies in [0.80, 0.90].

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. 'refutes' if the regular fraction is below 0.70 or above 0.95. 'mixed' if it lies in [0.70, 0.80) or (0.90, 0.95]. 'inconclusive' with reason 'other' if the calibration fails to separate the reference classes (largest nested rho >= smallest irregular rho). The number of irregular codes that are random-looking (rho above the smallest random reference) versus structured-irregular is reported but not decisive.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: fraction of the 2187 codes classified regular (late-time strip periodic with p <= 256, or rho < tau)

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: deterministic given tau = 0.060; a few long-transient codes may be misclassified at T = 3000

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: 'Ultimately quite regular' is read as 'repetitive or nested at late times', operationalised as late-time periodicity of the central strip or compressibility at the level of classical nested patterns; 'the remainder' as everything compressing like random or localised-structure patterns, with elementary class-3 and class-4 rules from a different family used to fix the threshold. 'About 85 %' is given a +/- 5 percentage-point band. Long transients (Wolfram mentions code 1599 resolving only after thousands of steps) may leave a few ultimately regular codes labelled irregular at T = 3000, which biases the regular fraction downward slightly. All patterns are generated by analysis.py; there is no external download.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: All 2187 three-colour nearest-neighbour totalistic cellular automata (Wolfram code numbering) from a single gray cell, 3000 steps, generated by analysis.py, plus the calibration reference patterns described in pass_criterion

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The regular/irregular split depends on tau, which is calibrated on elementary (2-colour) reference rules; the gap between the nested references (max 0.037) and the structured-irregular references (min 0.099) is wide and the census has no codes between 0.042 and 0.119, so the fraction is insensitive to the exact value of tau within that gap.

The pre-registered 'random-like' sub-count (rho above the smallest 2-colour random reference, 1.11) is not comparable across alphabets and came out as 0; the post-hoc quantiles added to measured.extra show 169 of the 336 irregular codes have rho >= 0.9, i.e. compress essentially like random 3-colour data. This sub-count was pre-registered as non-decisive.

T = 3000 steps: codes with transients longer than about 750 steps in the periodicity window, or whose late-time structure first appears beyond 3000 steps (NKS mentions code 1599 at thousands of steps), may be misclassified; code 1599 is counted irregular here (rho 0.55).

Codes are classified from a single gray cell only, as in the book's figure; a black-cell start would give a different census.

'About 85 %' is Wolfram's rounded figure; the pre-registered band [0.80, 0.90] was chosen to allow +/- 5 points of classification ambiguity. The measured 84.6 % lands within 0.4 points of the quoted figure.

Periodicity and compressibility are measured on the central 128 columns only; patterns whose irregularity is confined to the edges of the growing region (and whose centre is periodic) count as regular.
